The Philippine government continues to develop a globally competitive workforce by prioritizing solutions to address educational gaps in the country.

Outlined in the Executive Report 2026: Making 2026 a Rally Point to Revitalize PDP Implementation, the government aims to address key challenges such as high learning poverty, frequent class suspensions, and inadequate learning resources and facilities. Preparing our children for the future requires ensuring that learning inputs, both in quantity and quality, are adequate and responsive to the needs of Filipino learners.

PUBLIC ADVISORY 📢

Dry Run for the Implementation of Parking Regulation for Public Parking Space (Tomas Morato - Timog Avenue)

In line with the QC ReVibe beautification efforts in the city’s tourist districts, the Quezon City Government will be conducting a dry run for the implementation of parking regulations along Tomas Morato Avenue and Timog Avenue starting tomorrow, March 23, 2026.

1. Parking in public parking areas will be FREE, on a first-come, first-served basis.
2. Vehicles will be allowed to park for a maximum of three (3) hours, after which, drivers must move their vehicles to a different public parking spot.
3. Parking tickets will be issued by attendants from the QC Transport and Traffic Management Department (TTMD) only. No other person can issue or collect any parking ticket.
4. Once three (3) hours have passed and the driver has not complied, TTMD attendants will issue a violation.
5. Collection of parking fees in any form is strictly prohibited and may be reported to the TTMD main office.

This parking regulation shall remain in effect until the passage of the PUBLIC PAY PARKING ORDINANCE. 

Thank you for your cooperation and understanding.

Link to initial advisory post: https://t.co/tBmevlrfSM
